statement.p: The temperature at any point in the plane is given by \displaystyle T(x,y) = \frac{130}{x^{2}+y^{2}+1}.

(a) What shape are the level curves of T?
parabolas
circles
hyperbolas
lines
ellipses
none of the above
(b) At what point on the plane is it hottest?
(c) Find the direction of the greatest increase in temperature at the point (-1,1).
What is the value of this maximum rate of change, that is, the maximum value of the directional derivative at (-1,1)?
(d) Find the direction of the greatest decrease in temperature at the point (-1,1).
What is the value of this most negative rate of change, that is, the minimum value of the directional derivative at (-1,1)?

solution.p: (a) Let k >0 be constant. The level curves have equation k =\frac{130}{x^{2}+y^{2}+1} or x^2 + y^2 = \frac{130}{k} - 1. If \frac{130}{k} - 1 > 0, these equations represent circles in the xy- plane.
(b) The largest value of the temperature T is attained at (0,0).
The value of the temperature at this point is T(0,0) = \frac{130}{1}=130
(c) The greatest increase in temperature at (-1,1) is in the direction of the gradient at the point.
(c) The greatest decrease in temperature at (-1,1) is in the opposite direction of the gradient at the point: -\nabla f(-1, 1) = - \left\lt 28.8889,-28.8889\right>
